§2Solution Overview

C4 — Level 2: Containers (sourced: architecture-c4.md — real codebase)

C4 Level 2 — Containers (real services from health-care-project): gateway · app · governance · rules · payment · payment-worker · OCR · HL7 · PostgreSQL 16 · Redis 7

Architecture diagram (sourced: health-care-project/documents/architect.drawio — rendered)

Full architecture diagram (AWS — LLMOps platform · EKS · rotation · multi-cloud) — rendered from architect.drawio, embedded as SVG

Microservices & messaging (real inventory — health-care-project/apps)

15 backend services + web frontend + storybook: auth-service · tenant-service · user-service · catalog-service · clinic-service · ehr-service · eligibility-service · rules-service · governance · payment-service · payment-worker · notification-worker · hl7-integration · ocr-document-processor · gateway · web. Event backbone: Redis 7 + Kafka (docker-compose) — queues, cache, sessions, events.

Payment flow (sourced: payment-service/README.md + payment-worker/README.md): Payment Service (NestJS) orchestrates Stripe with webhook idempotency and a transactional outbox; the Payment Worker is the thin async trampoline consuming outbox events — decoupled, retryable, no data loss. Rules Service drives eligibility/estimation via rule-engine-contracts.

Infrastructure structure — topology

Infrastructure structure — AWS Cloud → VPC → gateway → 15 services → data (PostgreSQL 16 · Redis 7 · Kafka) → externals (Cognito · SES · S3 · OfficeAlly · Stripe · EHR)

Scaling (sourced: payment architecture)

The outbox + worker pattern is the scaling backbone: Payment Service writes to the transactional outbox (atomic with the DB transaction); Payment Worker consumes independently — horizontal scale by worker count, no payment loss, retryable. Redis 7 hosts queues/cache/sessions.
